newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eurotunnel reaches outline debt deal.
newsitem.headline: Eurotunnel reaches outline debt deal.

text.p: Channel Tunnel operator Eurotunnel SA/Plc reached an outline agreement with six bank lenders on Tuesday to restructure debt and unpaid interest totalling some 70 billion francs ($14 billion), a source familiar with the marathon negotiations said.
"There has been a global agreement, the details are being finalised this evening," the source told Reuters.
A Eurotunnel spokeswoman declined comment. In London, National Westminster Bank Plc said talks were continuing but it was optimistic.

Eurotunnel's co-chairmen Alistair Morton and Patrick Ponsolle have been in intense negotiations with bankers to break a deadlock over the pricing of a debt-for-equity swap and issue of convertible bonds needed to lighten its debt service.
The president of the Paris commercial court, Jean-Pierre Mattei, was expected to make a statement either on Tuesday night or Wednesday on the debt talks which have been stalled for a year.

Eurotunnel, which operates the rail tunnel opened in May 1994, froze interest payments on its junior-ranked debt in September 1995, unable to bear the debt burden incurred due to cost overruns incurred digging the Franco-British link.
